title: “WHAT CAN YOU GIVE ME?”
paragraphs: “WHAT CAN YOU GIVE ME?”
Silence from heaven can feel like betrayal.
Years earlier, God had spoken a promise over a wandering man named Abraham.

A future.
A nation.
Descendants like stars.
But in Book of Genesis chapter 15, the promise still looked impossible.

No son.
No heir.
No evidence.
Just waiting.
Abraham finally said what many believers whisper but rarely admit:

“Lord God… what can You give me, since I remain childless?”
— Genesis 15:2
Not rebellion.
Honesty.
Faith sometimes asks questions with trembling hands.

Waiting stretches the soul.
Every silent year pulls the promise tighter against doubt.

And Abraham had a reasonable backup plan:
His servant, Eliezer of Damascus.
If God’s promise didn’t arrive… he would make his own solution.
Human logic.
Practical.
Safe.
But heaven interrupted.
God brought Abraham outside.
Into the night.

No temple.
No throne room.
Just sky.
And the Lord said:

“Look toward heaven and count the stars—if you are able to count them.”
— Genesis 15:5
Then came the impossible line:
“So shall your offspring be.”
Stars where Abraham saw emptiness.
Promise where Abraham saw delay.
And then Scripture drops one of the most powerful sentences in the entire Bible:

“Abram believed the Lord, and He credited it to him as righteousness.”
— Genesis 15:6
Not perfection.
Not performance.
Faith.
Centuries later, the apostle Paul the Apostle would point back to this very moment to explain the Gospel.
Righteousness comes by faith.
Not by earning.
Not by human effort.
But by trusting the promise of God fulfilled in Jesus Christ.
Here’s the secret many believers miss:
Waiting is not punishment.
Waiting is where faith learns to breathe.
God was not ignoring Abraham.
God was building a story so large that when the promise finally arrived, the only explanation would be grace.
And when Isaac was born years later, every cry of that baby shouted the same truth:
God keeps His word.
Maybe tonight you’re asking the same question Abraham asked:
“Lord… what can You give me?”

A marriage still barren.
A dream still delayed.
A prayer that feels unanswered.
Hear this, friend.
The God who counted stars for Abraham has not forgotten your name.
At the center of every promise stands the cross of Jesus Christ—where God proved once and for all that He does not abandon those who trust Him.
Your waiting is not wasted.
Your faith is not unseen.
And the same grace that justified Abraham still saves today.

Turn to Christ.
Trust His promise.
And watch how God writes redemption into the places where doubt once lived.
🔥 We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
